item.title: 50Hertz: Cloud-Native Quality Engineering
item.description:
50Hertz Project Background Summary

By 2032, 50Hertz aims to integrate an annual average of 100 percent renewable energies safely into the grid and the system. Digital transformation plays a decisive role in achieving this ambitious goal.

To support this transition, 50Hertz is developing a new grid control system designed to manage the complexities of renewable energy integration and ensure grid stability.

My Role in the 50Hertz Project

I worked as the Quality Assurance (QA) Lead for one product line in the 50Hertz project. Working closely with development engineers and system architects, I connected test strategy, automation, CI/CD feedback, and Kubernetes-based validation for a critical grid-control product.

Key Responsibilities

  • Led quality engineering efforts to ensure software reliability and delivery confidence throughout the development lifecycle.
  • Combined manual and automated testing in a CI/CD environment to give teams timely quality feedback.
  • Validated application scalability and compatibility within Kubernetes clusters.
  • Conducted UI/UX testing to optimize the user experience and improve usability.

This engagement demonstrated how hands-on QA leadership, test automation, and cloud-native validation can strengthen the robustness of systems supporting 100% renewable integration into the grid.

item.title: Banking: Test Automation & Compliance Quality
item.description:
Banking Sector Project Background

This project was carried out for one of the largest banks in Germany, with a strong focus on quality assurance and test automation. The goal was to meet regulatory requirements efficiently while improving software quality in the area of document generation.

My Role in the Banking Sector Project

As the Test Manager, I led cross-functional initiatives to automate testing processes and managed test-data preparation for the creation and validation of audit-relevant documents. The role combined quality leadership with practical automation and delivery-risk management in a regulated environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Led test automation initiatives to reduce manual efforts and increase efficiency.
  • Managed test data preparation for the automated generation and validation of audit-compliant documents.
  • Enhanced test coverage and optimized test processes to identify risks early and make quality controls repeatable.
  • Aligned cross-functional stakeholders on reliable quality practices for audit-relevant delivery.

Through this project, I helped make quality assurance more efficient, repeatable, and reliable in a highly regulated banking environment.

item.title: Quorivell: Local-First Decisions with On-Device AI
item.description:
Hobby project

I work as a freelance DevOps / quality engineering consultant by day. Quorivell is a personal Flutter side project: a private, local-first app that turns messy conversation text into reviewable decisions and commitments — with evidence kept on the device.

Tagline: Decisions, with evidence — on your device.

What it does

  • Capture conversation text as source records
  • Extract candidates on-device with a local GGUF model (llama.cpp)
  • Review before anything is saved — nothing auto-writes the ledger
  • Ledger for decisions, commitments, owners, and due dates you can audit
  • Chat in free-form threads on the same local model
  • Locales: English, German, and Arabic (Material 3)

Privacy is the product: Drift SQLite on device is canonical, inference stays local, and source content does not leave the phone unless you later opt into an explicit remote flow.

Stack (short)

Flutter · Riverpod · GoRouter · Drift · Freezed · llama.cpp (llama_cpp_dart) · Firebase Auth foundation (no cloud AI for capture/extract)

Links

  • GitHub: cherifsahraoui/Quorivell
  • Google Play (closed testing): com.quorivell.app

Under active development — expect sharp edges, especially around large on-device model downloads.

item.title: Volkswagen Infotainment: Integration & Test Automation
item.description:
Volkswagen Infotainment Project Background Summary

Volkswagen Infotainment GmbH, located in Bochum, Germany, is responsible for delivering advanced infotainment systems that enhance the driving experience. These systems integrate cutting-edge technologies to provide seamless connectivity, entertainment, and navigation features for Volkswagen’s range of vehicles.

My Role in the Volkswagen Infotainment Project

From June 2021 to August 2022, I worked as a System Integration and Test Engineer for the Volkswagen Infotainment project. In this role, I collaborated closely with internal and external partners, including Volkswagen and Continental, to integrate, verify, and deliver complex embedded and cloud-connected software systems.

Key Responsibilities

  • Analyzed requirements and defined software-integration and test criteria, identifying testability and integration risks early.
  • Developed and implemented software, integration, and system tests with a focus on test automation and reliable regression feedback.
  • Developed CI workflows and integration pipelines for complex embedded and cloud-connected systems.
  • Collaborated with internal and external partners (Volkswagen, Continental) to ensure smooth integration and resolve issues.
  • Tracked issues and progress in Jira, ensuring timely resolutions.

This work combined systems engineering, test automation, and CI-enabled feedback to support the reliable delivery of advanced infotainment technology.
